title: Dynamic Equilibrium
short: At equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions run at equal rates, so the amounts stop changing.
trouble: Students think the reactions stop at equilibrium, or that the reactants and products must be present in equal amounts.

blocks.html: Many reactions can run backward too. In a sealed flask, the products of colliding reactants collide with each other and re-form the reactants. What happens when both directions run at once?

A reversible reaction reaches equilibrium when the forward and reverse reactions run at equal rates. From then on the amounts of reactants and products stay constant, though both reactions keep going. Constant does not mean equal: the amounts can be very different.

At the start only reactants are present, so the forward reaction is fast and the reverse reaction cannot run. As reactants are used up, the forward rate falls; as products build up, the reverse rate rises. The two rates meet, and after that each molecule of product that forms is matched by one that turns back. It is like a crowded shop where people enter and leave at the same rate: the number inside holds steady while the people keep changing.

blocks.name: ch-equilibrium
blocks.cap: Starting with only A. The forward rate falls and the reverse rate rises until they are equal; after that the concentrations stop changing, but they are not equal.

blocks.name: ch-particles
blocks.cap: The particle view: molecules keep reacting in both directions, while the counts of each kind stay about the same.

blocks.title: Not equal, just constant
blocks.q: A flask starts with $1.00\ \text{M}$ of A and no B. At equilibrium, $[\mathrm{A}] = 0.25\ \text{M}$ for $\mathrm{A} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{B}$. What is $[\mathrm{B}]$?
steps: Each A that reacts becomes one B.
The two stay at $0.25$ and $0.75\ \text{M}$ while molecules keep switching back and forth.

blocks.title: Using the coefficients
blocks.q: A flask starts with $1.00\ \text{M}$ of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$. At equilibrium in $$2\mathrm{NO}_{2} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$$ $[\mathrm{N_2O_4}] = 0.30\ \text{M}$. What is $[\mathrm{NO_2}]$?

blocks.html: Thinking the reactions stop at equilibrium, or that the reactants and products must be present in equal amounts. Both reactions continue; only the rates are equal. Check: "equilibrium" is about rates being equal, not amounts.
